newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cambodia's Rainsy seeks halt to Australian aid.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Rainsy seeks halt to Australian aid.

text.p: Cambodian opposition leader Sam Rainsy said on Wednesday he would lobby Australian leaders next week to halt aid to Cambodia and insist on free and fair elections in the troubled Southeast Asian nation.

Rainsy, a former finance minister in Cambodia's ruling coalition, said Cambodians needed international help and protection after Second Prime Minister Hun Sen ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh last month.
"Cambodia under Hun Sen's oppressive regime will not stabilise," Rainsy said in a statement released here ahead of his visit to Australia next week. Rainsy is in Bangkok.
Rainsy will press Foreign Minister Alexander Downer to halt aid to Cambodia, which relies heavily on foreign assistance, a spokesman for Rainsy told Reuters.
He will also meet other government and community leaders during a five-day visit to Australia to seek support.

Australia last month put its A$2.0 million (US$1.5 million) Cambodian military aid programme on hold and warned Hun Sen that A$32 million of general aid could also be stopped in protest at Hun Sen's military-backed action.

Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) formed an uneasy coalition with Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993. But the partnership faltered in recent months, leading up to Hun Sen's military seizure of power.
Cambodia's National Assembly on Wednesday approved FUNCINPEC Foreign Minister Ung Huot as Ranariddh's replacement as first prime minister.
Rainsy, who formed his own Khmer Nation Party after quitting FUNCINPEC, won international praise as finance minister and for his anti-corruption campaigning after the 1993 election.
Rainsy and his party are now part of a Khmer opposition coalition that condemned Ung Huot's appointment as illegal.
